title: The Eleven Stars That Bowed
intro: A figure from the Quran was granted a profound vision in childhood — a dream of celestial bodies bowing in reverence. Years would pass through betrayal, separation, false accusation, and imprisonment before this vision came true. Who is this resilient soul whose story occupies the longest chapter of the Quran?
clues: I was once young, blessed with a remarkable dream that even my own father warned me to keep private.
My own brothers, blinded by jealousy, plotted against me and cast me into a deep, dark well.
I was carried to a distant land and sold into the household of a noble official, where I found favor and rose in responsibility.
False accusation led to my unjust imprisonment, yet in that dark place I found solace in prayer and prostration to Allah.
Allah blessed me with the rare ability to interpret dreams, which eventually brought me before the ruler of the land and elevated me to a high position of trust.
After long years of separation, I was reunited with my beloved family, and my childhood dream of eleven stars, the sun, and the moon bowing to me was finally fulfilled.

outcome.answer: Reunited with family after years of separation and became a trusted minister

arabic: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى ٱشْتَرَىٰهُ مِن مِّصْرَ لِٱمْرَأَتِهِۦٓ أَكْرِمِى مَثْوَىٰهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًۭا ۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَكَّنَّا لِيُوسُفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلِنُعَلِّمَهُۥ مِن تَأْوِيلِ ٱلْأَحَادِيثِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَالِبٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرِهِۦ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
verse: And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son." And thus, We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events [i.e., dreams]. And Allāh is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know. (12:21)
